A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RaPA research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original targeted-attack experiments, parameter-importance measurements, ablations, defense evaluations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds experiments with newer surrogate models, ImageNet-V2, multiple surrogate models, and untargeted attacks.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, Bernoulli parameter masking, selected layer types, and gradient aggregation remain unchanged. The additional evaluations do not document a new RaPA component or revised pruning procedure.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates targeted attacks on the ImageNet-compatible dataset. v3 Appendix D.4 adds ImageNet-V2 evaluation and actual untargeted-attack results, substantially extending both distribution and task coverage.

E2.justification: Diversity Weight Pruning (DWP), previously discussed without reported results, becomes an evaluated comparator in Tables 3, 4, and 8. Existing comparators remain; CFM and FTM were already evaluated in v2.

E3.justification: Appendix D.4 introduces MambaVision-T, DINOv2-Large, and ConvNeXtV2-L surrogate configurations, plus a five-source ensemble evaluated against six Transformer targets. These substantially extend the evaluation design beyond individual surrogates. The previously reported Section 4.1 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds distribution-shift evaluation on ImageNet-V2, single-versus-multiple-source comparisons, and source-to-source versus transfer results for newer surrogates to examine overfitting. These extend the robustness analyses beyond v2's retained pruning, layer, probability, compute-budget, defense, and visualization studies.

E5.justification: The existing ± entries in Tables 3–4 remain unchanged, and no new run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedure are documented. The new assertion that untargeted results are statistically indistinguishable supplies no test or uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: v3 adds DWP scores, Tables 11–12, and ensemble and untargeted findings while retaining existing numerical results. For example, new ImageNet-V2 ViT-to-CNN ASRs are 73.0% for RaPA, 56.6% for CFM, and 20.3% for FTM; the five-source ensemble achieves 63.3% versus CFM's 60.7%. These are additional settings, not improvements over v2 under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: The parameter-importance definition, masked-loss approximation, Appendix B derivation, and Gini definitions are retained. Added parentheses around loss arguments in Equations (3) and (7) clarify notation without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about parameter over-reliance, random pruning, importance equalization, transferability, and compute scaling. The headline performance claims are unchanged; new experiments provide additional support.

C2.justification: Appendix D.4 adds interpretations concerning CFM overfitting, generalization across datasets and ensembles, and untargeted saturation as a reason to emphasize targeted evaluation. It removes v2's explicit limitation about low CLIP-to-CNN success rates, although the corresponding low scores remain in Table 9.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and repository URL to the abstract. Existing implementation instructions and hyperparameters remain, while the added experiments receive only limited configuration details.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for MambaVision, DINOv2, ConvNeXt V2, and ImageNet-V2 to support the expanded evaluation. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing attack methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language corrections, shortens Section 4.5, adds an affiliation and acknowledgements, and introduces appendix subheadings with corresponding renumbering. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 11–12, inserts DWP rows in Tables 3–4 and a DWP column in Table 8, and relocates Table 5 and Figure 7 through reflow. Existing figures retain their visual content; there is no broad redesign.

improvement.justification: The added generalization experiments and direct DWP comparisons strengthen empirical support beyond v2, and the code pointer improves access information. These gains are qualified by sparse reporting of the new protocols, an unsupported statistical-indistinguishability assertion, and removal of the explicit CLIP-to-CNN limitation despite unchanged low scores. The net improvement is useful but limited.
